items.item_text: Education acceptable by the California Board of Nursing to obtain required licensure.
At the NP 1 Level: Newer NP's with clinic experience as an RN may be considered
Patient care experience in a pediatrics or primary care setting.
At the NP 2 Level: A minimum of two years' experience as a Nurse Practitioner.
Must meet UC credentialing requirements.

Direct Patient Care: 1.Obtain thorough histories and perform complete physical examinations, including ordering, interpreting, and evaluating tests and examinations. Perform well child visits. Order immunizations per the AAP (American Academy of Pediatrics) guidelines. 2. Assume ongoing responsibility for each patient. 3. Diagnose and treat both chronic and episodic disorders including complications of otherwise normal processes. Referrals to other physicians or treatment options.4. Establish and document the health care plan and diagnosis, maintain records of each case that are sufficiently complete for any provider or physician reviewing them to evaluate the effectiveness of the plan. 5. Monitor and evaluate patients in the ambulatory setting with new or ongoing issues. Facilitate transitions of care and care coordination. May communicate with hospitalists and other physicians on patient care. 6. Review and respond to lab/test results, patient Inbasket/MyChart messages, staff messages, refill requests, telephone calls, and virtual patient encounters. 7. Follow department/clinic guidelines for providing continuity of care in collaboration and coordination with physician. 8. Complete all patient care and encounter documentation in the electronic health record system promptly per policy. 9. Coordinate/recommend follow up with appropriate laboratory tests, imaging and diagnostic studies, and consults/referrals. 10. Provide care to achieve quality, safety, efficiency, and patient experience goals. Incumbent will demonstrate a caring, sensitive, and service approach in all interactions with patients, families, and the health care team; 11. Demonstrates proficiency in the use of EHR, computers, and telecommunication systems; consistently demonstrates the knowledge, skills, abilities, and behaviors necessary to provide superior and culturally sensitive service to each other, to our patients, and to, contracted providers, and vendors. 12. Collaborate extensively wit (70% time)

Provides patient/family member education promoting health maintenance, diabetes education, condition-based education including education on minimizing stress, maximizing wellness, encouraging health lifestyle changes, and identifying resources. Screen, address, and counsel on social drivers of health. Educates patients, parents, and caregivers on vaccines and addresses vaccine questions. (20% time)
Develops and provides educational materials and clinical instructions to other staff providing direct patient care. Serves as a lead for staff to address patient care issues and concerns. (10% time)
Current California Registered Nurse and Nurse Practitioner license.
Current unrestricted DEA license and National Provider Identifier (NPI) number.

Other: Must be able to lift up to and push / pull 50 pounds. Must be able to assist patients with mobility during rooming patients and in preparation for exams/procedures. Able to respond to assist in emergency scenarios; administer CPR and ACLS.
Strong interpersonal skills and excellent bedside manner.
Ability to make emergency decisions quickly.
